delivery: Stay level and curious, with no sarcasm back.

text: Fair challenge. Let me show you rather than tell you.
delivery: Calm and unhurried. Then follow through.

text: I'd value your honest view, even if it's blunt.
delivery: Mean it, and listen to the whole answer.

text: Your standards are high, and I'd like to meet them.
delivery: Say it only if it's true. Even pace, no flattery.

text: It's good having you part of this. Your voice adds something.
I've really enjoyed doing this with you. Thank you for being part of it.
It's good having you here. Come along next time if you fancy it.
delivery: Use "we" and "us" language and say it with a smile.
ctx: No pressure either way.

text: Lots of people start right where you are. If it helps, I can share what worked for people I know.
ctx: Only say this if it is true.

text: There's more than one right way to do this, and yours makes sense.
You clearly put a lot into this group. I can see why people value you.
ctx: Only if it is true. Be specific about what you have seen.

text: Here are two options, or we can do neither. What would you like?
ctx: Saying no to both is a real option.

text: You mentioned ___ there. Is there more to that?
delivery: Listen for threads: a flash of emotion, a shift in tone. Follow gently, and let it go if they don't want to go there.
ctx: They can say no. Don't push.

text: Is there more you'd like to say about that? No pressure.
delivery: Soft voice, plenty of pause. This opens a door but never pulls them through it.
ctx: They can say no. Don't push.

text: That's a lot to have carried. What's helped you most so far?
delivery: Acknowledge first and pause, then gently move the conversation on.

text: Thank you for telling me. That sounds hard. What would make the next bit easier?
delivery: Acknowledge first and pause, then gently move the conversation on.

text: That sounds really heavy. How are you doing with it now?
delivery: Slow down, lower volume a little, pause after the first line. Don't minimise it, then gently move on.

text: You've come through a lot to get here, and it shows in how you handle things.
delivery: Sincere and unhurried. Avoid 'it's not that bad'. Then let the conversation move on.

text: That's a sharp point. What made you think of it?
You've clearly thought this through. Your reasoning holds up.
I'd value your read on this. What would you do?
delivery: Only say this if you mean it. Ask, then listen to the full answer.

text: You'll see it before anything is final, and I'll flag anything that needs your call.
ctx: Only promise what you can deliver.

text: I'll keep you updated at each step, so nothing comes as a surprise.
ctx: Only promise what you can deliver.

text: I take your standards seriously. Tell me what "right" looks like for you.
delivery: Level voice, steady eye contact.

text: That's a surprise! What's going through your mind?
delivery: Surprise fades in seconds. Ask while it is fresh, and smile if it is good news.

text: What was that like?
delivery: Ask, then stop. Let them take their time.
ctx: A follow-up question. Follow-ups raise liking.

text: How did that happen?
delivery: Ask, then stop. Let them take their time.
ctx: A follow-up question.

text: Why that one?
delivery: Light and curious, not testing.
ctx: A follow-up question.

text: Is your family from around here?
ctx: FORD topic: Family. Skip it if they seem private.

text: What are you working on at the moment?
ctx: FORD topic: Occupation.

text: What do you do to switch off?
ctx: FORD topic: Recreation.

text: If you had a free year, what would you do with it?
ctx: FORD topic: Dreams.

text: What do you do in your free time?
delivery: Ask it warmly, then follow the thread they give you.
ctx: Vinh's favourite question.

text: Are you upset? I might have that wrong.
delivery: Name the feeling gently and let them correct you.

text: Do we both want the same thing here?
delivery: Calm, curious tone. Then pause.

text: It's completely fine to change your mind. We both know more now than we did.
ctx: A dignified way to back down (a "golden bridge").

text: You made a fair call with what you knew then. Let's look at it fresh.
ctx: A dignified way to back down.

text: I can't do that, but here's what I can do: ___.
ctx: When you say no, offer something else.

text: Let's both sleep on it. There's no need to decide today.
ctx: A dignified way to pause.

text: Thanks, I'll come to that in a moment.
delivery: Warm, not sharp. Keep going, then come back to them.
ctx: If someone cuts in.

text: Give me five minutes to share the whole idea, then I'd love your input.
Enough about me. What would make this useful for you?
delivery: Nervous? Breathe out slowly, name it to yourself ("that's nerves"), then think about them, not you.
ctx: Vinh: nerves fade when you think about the other person.

text: Does this {feel/sound/look} right to you?
delivery: Match their words: "feel" if they talk in feelings, "sound" if they talk in sounds, "look" if they talk in pictures.

text: Does that {feel/sound/look} like the right fit?
delivery: Match their words, then pause and let them answer.

text: That {feels/sounds/looks} really important to you.
delivery: Slow down on "important".

text: How does that {feel/sound/look} to you?
delivery: Ask, then stop. Let them decide.
